description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
Random init again, printing sample task examples to learn the prompt/answer format.

Same-digit attention at the target gives 1/(k+1) on itself (softmax is the counter); second attention layer copies it to the answer positions; ReLU MLP interpolates through the 11 values. One-hot digits, d_model=17, no LayerNorm.
Digits on a 2D Fourier circle: same-digit attention is a cosine; softmax counter gives 1/(k+1); MLP interpolates a circle vector read by a weight-tied head. d_model=7.
No MLP at all: softmax counter, then the head is a nearest-prototype classifier (lines tangent to rho^2) on the count register; the echoed tens token picks units for count 10. d_model=6.
Same circuit as NoMLPTangentHeadD6 with the W_o projections removed and the positional table cut to the 13 positions used. d_model=6.
One signed flag replaces the position flags (+1 target, -1 answer), so layer 2 finds the target by sign; '=' is placed off the circle to give the head its tens bias. d_model=4.
The signed flag dim also holds the count. Answer positions sit off the unit circle so they self-attend in layer 1, leaving their flag at exactly -2 before reading the target. d_model=3.
Same circuit as FlagIsRegisterD3 with q, k, v as per-dim gains instead of matrices: every attention weight is now a channel gain. Single head. d_model=3.
Positional table replaced by two marks (target at 10, answer echo at 12); the -1 flag at position 11 lives in the '=' token itself. d_model=3.
Head has 10 rows, so '=' cannot be emitted and needs no suppression weight. Otherwise TwoMarksNoPosTable. d_model=3.
Attention is a bilinear metric per layer, score = x diag(m) x', with the value fixed to the flag channel: 6 attention numbers in total, in score units. d_model=3.
Sharpness sweep: MetricAttention with the attention score margin lowered from 40 to 10, so non-matches leak about e^-10 of attention.
Sharpness sweep: MetricAttention with the attention score margin lowered to 4, so non-matches leak about e^-4 of attention each.
Sharpness sweep: MetricAttention with the attention score margin lowered to 2, so non-matches leak about e^-2 of attention each. Expected to break the count.
Head uses tangents of 1/rho rather than rho^2: logit_u = 2n - n^2 rho with n = u+1, integer weights and a far larger logit margin. Attention margin 10. d_model=3.
Digits placed at the third harmonic (108 degrees apart), testing that numeric adjacency on the circle plays no part in the same-digit test. Otherwise ReciprocalTangentHead.

Negative control: the tens digit is stuck at '0', so count 10 is deliberately wrong (self-check 7000/7200). The 1.0 only shows the 200-sample eval cannot see the tens path; this model is NOT a correct solution.
Negative control: layer 2 removed, so the answer positions cannot read the count held at the target. Tests whether two attention layers are necessary.
Robustness sweep: ReciprocalTangentHead with additive Gaussian noise of sigma 0.001 on every weight, zeros included.

Same 0.001 noise test with flag channel gain F=10 and logit gain C=1000. Hypothesis that this would help was wrong: accuracy fell. Cause not isolated; the -100 gate found later scales with C too, and flag noise grows with F.

Same 0.001 noise test with logit gain C=1000 only and F=1: self-check 6641/7200 vs 6621/7200 without gain, so a uniform logit gain does not help. (The -100 gate weight scales with C, see SoftGateB5Noise1e-3.)
All weights human-readable: metrics 50 and -15, '=' at (10/7, 1/2), circle rounded to 2 decimals, head in integers and half-integers. No derived constants. d_model=3.
Flag metric in layer 1 boosts the target's self-score by ln 5, so the code is rho = 5/(5+k), spreading high counts: the k=9/10 gap rises from 0.009 to 0.024. d_model=3.

Robustness test: BoostedSelfB5 under the same sigma 0.001 noise and seed as Noise1e-3. Self-check fell to 4733/7200 vs 6621/7200; first failures were on target 0, pointing at the -100 gate weight rather than the counter.

Tests the gate diagnosis: as BoostedSelfB5Noise1e-3 but with the digit gate weight softened from -100 to -10, same noise and seed. Self-check 6809/7200, up from 4733: diagnosis confirmed, though not error-free under noise.
Candidate design with no noise: boosted self-score (rho = 5/(5+k)), tangents of 1/rho in the head, and a -10 digit gate. d_model=3.
Robustness limit: SoftGateB5 with additive Gaussian noise of sigma 0.01 on every weight, zeros included.
Tolerance test: FinalSoftmaxCounterD3 with additive Gaussian noise of sigma 0.0003 on every weight, zeros included.

Final model: 2 attention layers, no MLP, d_model=3. Softmax over same-digit positions counts (rho = 5/(5+k)), answer positions read it, and argmax over tangents of 1/rho decodes it. All weights rounded and readable.
